text:
deploy-bot: CONFIG-ONLY deploy scheduled: 'driftshield' sweep starting now. change window 19:00-21:00 UTC. rolling canary: 5% -> 25% -> 100%. params: tenant_rate_limits, request_timeout_ms, routing_weight, batch_window_ms, kv_cache_warmup=true. :rocket:
alex: copying the config diff here — can we confirm the precise timeout delta?
marta: +1 — why are we increasing per-tenant floor for small tenants? risk to bursty workloads?
jordan: link to perf baseline dashboards: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/driftshield-baseline :eyes:
sre-oncall: quick ask — set auto-rollback triggers pls: 95p latency > 250ms OR error_rate > 0.5% for 5m => rollback. Also alert channel #incidents.
deploy-bot: ack. auto-rollback thresholds set. canary rollout step 1 -> 5% now.
alex: pasted minimal diff for ops review:
```json
{"tenant_rate_limits": {"min_rps": 0.5, "max_rps": 50}, "request_timeout_ms": 12000, "routing_weight": {"primary": 0.9, "fallback": 0.1}, "batch_window_ms": 8, "kv_cache_warmup": true}
```
marta: timeout from 10s -> 12s makes sense for long-tail LLMs, ok. batch_window 8ms is new, was 5ms before — any reason?
jordan: increasing batch_window to 8ms smooths spikes and reduces token cost. we've simulated 10% cost drop in replay.
sre-oncall: please confirm memory headroom on dedicated pools — kv warmup increases mem by ~200MB per shard. if heap pressure > 70% at canary step, halt.
deploy-bot: canary step 1 completed: 5% stable for 6m. metrics: 95p latency 185ms (baseline 178ms), error_rate 0.08%. no alerts. moving to 25% in 3m. :thumbsup:
alex: tagging @marta — if 25% shows kv cache thrash we should pin to previous routing weight and fallback to soft-throttle.
marta: agreed. fallback plan: immediately set routing_weight.primary=0.8 and batch_window_ms=5, then unwind kv warmup flag.
jordan: adding a watch for kvcache_miss_rate and tail_latency against baseline. I'll post thresholds in 2m.
sre-oncall: reminder — deployer bot will post rollback call if thresholds breach. ops runbook: https://go/internal/runbooks/config-rollback
deploy-bot: canary step 2 -> 25% started. monitors: kvcache_miss_rate 0.9% (baseline 0.7%), 95p latency 192ms, cpu headroom 62%.
alex: those numbers look fine. continue but keep close watch.
marta: logging note — please capture a sample of requests with new routing_weight for regression evals.
jordan: will snapshot prompts and responses for 30m window and run eval suite.
sre-oncall: HOLD — noticing background OOMs on one dedicated host (host-12). marking 25% canary paused.
deploy-bot: canary paused at 25%. auto-rollback not triggered yet. initiating investigation hook.
alex: ok pause acknowledged. rollback not yet necessary but hold on further ramp. anyone on host-12?
marta: @jordan can you check pod logs and OOM killer traces?
jordan: pulling logs now. I see repeated alloc spikes from kv prefill, going to scale down warmup threads and restart shard on host-12.
sre-oncall: please do the soft fix: set kv_cache_warmup_threads=1 for host-12 (override) and reschedule. If OOMs persist after 2 restarts, rollback to previous config across canary.
deploy-bot: override applied to host-12: kv_cache_warmup_threads=1. restart initiated.
jordan: restart completed, host-12 stable for 3m, no OOMs. metrics returning to prior levels.
marta: thanks. resume canary when host-12 cleared from pause. propose slow ramp to 40% then 100%.
alex: +1. record change in release notes: "driftshield: per-tenant floors adjusted, 12s timeout, batch window 8ms, kv cache warmup introduced with host-level overrides for safety."
sre-oncall: add note: "auto-rollback thresholds and host override mechanism enabled."
deploy-bot: canary resumed to 40% at 1759130400. monitoring.
jordan: snapshot saved, running regression checks. no functional regressions seen in sample.
deploy-bot: canary completed to 100% at 1759130520. no rollback triggered. final status: SUCCESS. :tada:
alex: will follow up with post-deploy checklist tomorrow morning and open a small retro if any anomalies.
marta: good job. closing thread once release note PR merges. :white_check_mark:
